pageCache.text:
STRIVING FOR EXCELLENCE
At Thames View Junior School, we are a vibrant and inclusive learning community where children from diverse cultures and backgrounds come together to learn, grow and thrive. Our motto, “Striving for Excellence,” reflects our commitment to ensuring that every child feels valued, supported and inspired to achieve their very best.
Through high expectations, an ambitious curriculum and our shared core values, we develop confident, resilient and aspirational learners. By celebrating diversity, encouraging curiosity and fostering mutual respect, we prepare our pupils to embrace future opportunities and make a positive contribution to the wider world.
James Smith Executive Headteacher
Welcome to Thames View Junior School
I would like to warmly welcome you to our school. Our motto is ‘Striving for Excellence’. At the heart of everything we do is to make a difference to our children’s lives.
At Thames View Junior School, we aim to provide an excellent start to pupils' education: growing confidence and a love of learning within the context of excellent teaching; high expectations and a relevant, interesting, ambitious and engaging curriculum.
Thames View Juniors is a community school which is based in Barking within the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. We pride ourselves on providing a caring and friendly atmosphere associated with smaller schools.
We pride ourselves on not only our academic achievements but also our sporting opportunities, love of singing and performance and our planned events and trips to enrich the lives of our children.

BRITISH VALUES
Our School
British Values at Thames View Junior School
At Thames View Junior School, our motto is "Striving for Excellence", and our vision is to ensure that every child is valued, supported and inspired to reach their full potential. As a diverse and inclusive school community, we actively promote the fundamental British Values of Democracy, The Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, Mutual Respect, and Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs through our curriculum, enrichment opportunities and everyday school life. Our aim is to prepare pupils to become confident, responsible and respectful citizens who are ready to positively embrace life in modern Britain.
At Thames View Junior School, everybody has a voice and is valued. Positive relationships between staff, pupils and families help our children flourish in a safe and nurturing environment where respect, tolerance and ambition underpin everything we do. Our broad and balanced curriculum celebrates the rich diversity of our school community and helps pupils develop the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to thrive in a modern, multicultural society.
Democracy
The concept of pupil voice is central to life at Thames View Junior School. We believe children should have opportunities to contribute to decision-making and help shape their school experiences. Through these experiences, pupils develop an understanding of democratic processes and learn the importance of listening to different viewpoints.
We promote democracy through:
Elections of class representatives and School Ambassadors.
The Rule of Law
At Thames View Junior School, we help pupils understand that rules are essential for creating a safe, happy and successful community. Children learn that laws and rules protect individuals and promote fairness, helping everyone to make positive choices and understand the consequences of their actions.
We support this understanding through:
Clear school rules and consistent expectations.
Individual Liberty
We nurture pupils in a safe and supportive environment where they are encouraged to develop independence, confidence and resilience. Children are taught how to make informed choices, understand their rights and responsibilities, and recognise how their actions affect others.
We promote individual liberty through:
Comprehensive safeguarding and e-safety education.
Mutual Respect
Respect is a core value of our school community. We teach children the importance of kindness, empathy and consideration for others, helping them build positive relationships and contribute positively to society.
We cultivate mutual respect by:
Recognising and celebrating individual achievements and contributions.
Providing opportunities for collaborative learning and teamwork.
Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
As a proudly multicultural school, we actively encourage pupils to develop an understanding and appreciation of different cultures, religions, traditions and ways of life. We believe that learning about others helps children become compassionate, open-minded and respectful members of society.
We achieve this through:
A rich and engaging Religious Education curriculum.
Cultural celebrations, themed events and enrichment activities.
Preparing Children for Life in Modern Britain
Through our commitment to British Values, our curriculum and our school ethos, Thames View Junior School equips pupils with the knowledge, skills and character needed to become active, respectful and responsible citizens. We strive to ensure that every child leaves our school with the confidence to contribute positively to their community and the wider world, living out our motto of "Striving for Excellence" in all that they do.

Vision and Ethos
Our School
Vision
Thames View Junior School is at the heart of our community. It is a place where everybody has a voice and is valued. Positive relationships between staff, pupils and parents ensure that our children flourish in an environment of mutual respect and tolerance. We are an ambitious school with high expectations of both staff and pupils.
Our children will leave us, ready to positively embrace life in modern Britain and through our broad and balanced curriculum we endeavour to prepare them for the stage of their academic journey.
At Thames View Junior School, our safe and nurturing environment enables children to flourish and attain their potential both academically and socially.

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us | Thames View Junior School
pageCache.text:
About Us
‘Strive for Excellence’ is our school motto, and it reflects everything we do here at Thames View Junior School.
Thank you for visiting our website. We hope it gives you a sense of what makes Thames View Junior School such a special place to learn and grow.
Thames View Junior School is a four-form-entry school for children in Years 3 to 6. We are part of the Partnership Learning multi-academy trust and are based in Barking, within the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. Despite being a large junior school, we pride ourselves on maintaining the caring, friendly and welcoming atmosphere often associated with smaller schools.
We recognise that your child’s time at primary school is precious, and we are delighted to share this important stage of their journey with you. Our broad and engaging curriculum places a strong emphasis on essential knowledge and basic skills, while bringing learning to life in exciting and meaningful ways. We also provide opportunities for children to develop their creativity and artistic talents and to learn through experiences within our local community and beyond.
We are committed to ensuring the effective inclusion of children with a wide range of educational needs and abilities. Our excellent and dedicated team of teachers and support staff work hard every day to ensure that every child feels safe, valued and supported to achieve their very best.
Please explore our website to learn more about our school. Better still, if you are a prospective parent, carer or member of our community, we would be delighted to welcome you in person. I, or another member of our team, would be very happy to show you around.
We look forward to welcoming you to Thames View Junior School.
Mrs S. Sanghera Head of School
Our School

YEAR 3 WELCOME
Thames View Junior School believe in “Striving for Excellence” where our pupils are at the centre of all that we do.
The school staff are key to our vision. We value their diversity. We aim to ensure that each staff member in our school moves forward in their employment as a whole person, through continuous professional development.
The curriculum is rich and varied. We look to develop everyone’s knowledge, understanding and skills. Our provision centres on high quality learning opportunities, teaching and facilities for all, whilst rigorously tailoring learning to meet the distinctive needs of different groups of pupils. We strive for high standards of learning and achievement so that all pupils reach their potential. We share with pupils and parents about the progress their child is making.

We thank you in advance for your continued support.
Best wishes. The Year 3 Team

SPORTS PREMIUM FUNDING
At Thames View Junior School, we are passionate about keeping every pupil active and healthy. Our PE and Sports Premium funding for 2024–2025 helps us go further, providing more opportunities, better resources, and lasting improvements in sport and physical activity.
The funding supports us to:
We believe that high-quality PE and a rich variety of sporting opportunities don’t just build skills—they support wellbeing, teamwork, and success across all areas of school life.
Pupils on Roll (Yr 3-6)
To encourage active play during break and lunchtimes
Provide high quality and appropriate equipment for playground

EXTRA CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES
During school closures there are no extra curricular clubs on offer to the children.
At Thames View Junior School we run a wide and varied range of clubs throughout the week. We encourage all children to try out a club as it gives them the opportunity to meet new people and make friends. Extra curricular activities also widen and broaden children’s experiences outside of the classroom and are therefore an incredibly important part of their education.
Our clubs are run on a first come first serve basis. These are purchased by parents by using MCAS.
After school clubs run from 3:10-4:10.
Children attending clubs must have the correct kit (sports) and must be collected on time. If you are running late please make contact with the school office on 020 511 9240, option 2. Consistent lateness may result in your child losing their place at the club.
Club spaces must be purchased through MyChildAtSchool (MCAS). Relevant guides can be found on the Guides page.

Art Projects
Each half term Ms Uppal (out Art Lead) has assigned a project please see below some pictures from them.
Summer Art Competition
This Summer term, we ran an art competition for all children across the school.
The theme was ‘Summer’ and the entry could be in the form of a drawing, painting, collage, sculpture or photograph. The children may have wished to use a range of natural materials —being as creative as they liked!
I am proud to say the entries that were made to show us what Summer means to the children have been displayed in the front office for all to see and admire.
Last week the School Ambassadors presented the two winning entries with arty prizes!
I thank you for letting their imaginations shine brightly and bringing Summer to life through art!
Enjoy the sunny weather!

ECO-WARRIORS
Thames View Junior School is now home to our esteemed Eco Warriors! Recently elected by their peers, these dedicated members, two from each class, are committed to fostering a healthy, sustainable environment within our school community.
Their selection came after thoughtful pledges from the warriors, all eager to enact positive change. With their enthusiasm and passion, our Eco Warriors will spearhead initiatives aimed at promoting eco-conscious practices around the school.
To keep everyone informed and engaged, we’ll be sharing meeting minutes fortnightly, showcasing the innovative ideas and projects our Eco Warriors are bringing to life.

RACE AND SOCIAL JUSTICE (RSJ)
Race and Social Justice (RSJ)
At Thames View Junior School we aim to make diversity and anti-racism central to our curriculum and practice, so that everyone feels valued and accepted for who they are and knows they belong. We are proud that our pupils and staff represent the diversity in our local community.
We strive to provide a broad and diverse learning experience that promotes equal opportunity, diversity and inclusivity. As a Rights Respecting school, we encourage pupil voice and participation in achieving our visions and aims.
Our school is implementing the Barking and Dagenham Race & Social Justice Charter. This is part of the wider race and social justice project which aims to ensure that all our young people have the best possible start in life.
The aims of the project are:
• Students’ experience of school, educational outcomes and life chances must not be adversely impacted by ethnic background or racial group
• The staff and leadership of our schools and borough must reflect our diversity
• Schools’ curriculum must reflect and celebrate the diversity of our borough
This charter is also reflected in our school values of respect, cooperation, compassion, honesty and courage.
We want all our pupils to feel valued see themselves in books they read. Here are some recommended books from ARISE (Anti-Racism in School and Education). Many of these can be found in our school and classroom libraries.
Article 2 (non-discrimination) The Convention applies to every child without discrimination, whatever their ethnicity, sex, religion, language, abilities or any other status, whatever they think or say, whatever their family background.

SCHOOL AMBASSADORS
School Ambassadors
Our ambassadors were given the opportunity to give a speech on why they should be chosen, to their class mates. Only 2 per class could be chosen and all students voted anonymously for the 2 class ambassadors, they were also discouraged from voting for friends and to only vote for the speeches that they thought best.
On September 19th 2025 Local MP, Nesil Caliskan, came to our school and presented all ambassadors with their badges of office. She answered questions on her job, her experience and many other topics.
We were visited in 2023 by then MP, Margaret Hodge, to present the 2023/24 Ambassadors with their badges of office and in 2024 by MP Necil Caliskan as well.
